answer.rationale: A release 2 hours ago correlates with 90-minute p99 latency climb, and we have one intervention window. memory_b1 shows rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact; memory_b2 is critical to verify because it established that regional failover during heavy writes risks a replication gap and write loss—this makes failover dangerous in current conditions with settlement traffic at peak and writes heavy. The deployment timing matches the symptom onset. Rollback is the lowest-risk path: it reverts the suspected root cause without the write-safety hazards of failover, maintains our staged release pattern from memory_b6, and preserves the existing capacity we provisioned in memory_b3. Circuit breaker (memory_b4) and read replicas (memory_b5) are read-path optimizations and won't address write-path latency. Add capacity takes time we don't have. Standard experiment scale provides controlled validation before full commit.
